transcript.text: Good afternoon, Parkside Sports Centre. Are you here to join?
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Yes, I am. I've just moved to the area, and my doctor suggested I should do more exercise.
transcript.speaker: LINDA

transcript.text: Very sensible. Exercise can make a big difference, especially when you're on your feet all day.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: That's what I've heard, and I'd like to feel fitter.
transcript.speaker: LINDA

transcript.text: Wonderful. Let me take some details. Could I have your surname?
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: It's Okafor. That's O-K-A-F-O-R.
transcript.speaker: LINDA

transcript.text: Thanks. And what do you do for a living, Ms Okafor?
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: I'm a nurse at the city hospital. I work irregular shifts, so I need flexible opening hours.
transcript.speaker: LINDA

transcript.text: That must be a demanding job. Many of our members are nurses and doctors, and they often come after a night shift.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: It's hard to find the energy sometimes, which is why I want to start slowly.
transcript.speaker: LINDA

transcript.text: That's no problem. We open at six in the morning, which suits shift workers. Now, which type of membership would you like? We have standard, student and family.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: I think I'll take the standard one. I'm not a student any more, and I live alone.
transcript.speaker: LINDA

transcript.text: Okay. The standard membership is twenty-two pounds a month. Would you like to start immediately?
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Not quite. I'm on holiday for a week, so please start it on the first of May.
transcript.speaker: LINDA

transcript.text: First of May. Fine. Do you have any health conditions we should know about?
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Just mild asthma. I always carry my inhaler, but I thought you should know.
transcript.speaker: LINDA

transcript.text: Don't worry, plenty of our members have asthma, and the instructors are trained in first aid.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: That's reassuring. I wouldn't want to cause any problems.
transcript.speaker: LINDA

transcript.text: Thank you, that's important. I'll note it on your file. Now, let me tell you about the facilities. The pool is on the ground floor, and it's open until ten at night.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Is there a gym as well?
transcript.speaker: LINDA

transcript.text: Yes, on the first floor. You need to book an induction session, which is free. The next available one is on Thursday morning.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: I'll take that. What about classes?
transcript.speaker: LINDA

transcript.text: We run yoga, spinning and a beginners' swimming class. Spinning is the most popular, so you need to reserve a place at least two days in advance.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: I've never tried spinning, but I think it could be fun.
transcript.speaker: LINDA

transcript.text: It's very energetic, but the instructors are friendly, and you can go at your own pace.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Okay. And is there somewhere to leave my belongings?
transcript.speaker: LINDA

transcript.text: We have lockers by the changing rooms. You need a one-pound coin, which you get back afterwards. Also, towels are not provided, so please bring your own.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Thank you. That's very helpful.
transcript.speaker: LINDA

transcript.text: That's everything for now. Come to the desk on Thursday and I'll show you around.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Great, see you then.
transcript.speaker: LINDA
